key_insight: Long-range ML interatomic potentials better capture electrostatic defect interactions in SrTiO3 than a short-range baseline, making them more suitable for charged-defect energetics and transport.
engineering_relevance: Accurate prediction of vacancy formation and migration barriers in perovskites can improve defect engineering, reliability, and ionic transport design for functional oxide materials.
method: Benchmarked MACE-POLAR, MACE-LES, and LOREM against short-range MACE
Started with synthetic point-charge systems, then moved to first-principles SrTiO3 defect data
Evaluated Sr–O Schottky pairs and oxygen-vacancy migration using CI-NEB and molecular dynamics
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a systematic benchmark spanning idealized electrostatic test cases and realistic DFT data, including vacancy-pair separation-dependent activation barriers.
watch_item: Long-range models still must disentangle Coulombic effects from DFT screening and other energy contributions, so gains may not transfer uniformly across materials or defect types.
paper_title: Long-Range Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials for Defect Energetics in SrTiO$_3$
